<ChapterHeader title="The CLI Manual" />

<Lead>
  For the power users, the keyboard-bound, and the automation-obsessed. The Opake CLI is the
  reference implementation of our protocol.
</Lead>

## Installation

The CLI is built in Rust and requires building from source. You'll need Rust 1.75+ and Git.

<CodeBlock language="sh">git clone https://tangled.org/sans-self.org/opake.app</CodeBlock>

<CodeBlock language="sh">cd opake.app && cargo install --path apps/cli</CodeBlock>

This puts the `opake` binary in your `~/.cargo/bin/` directory. Pre-built binaries and crates.io publishing are planned.

---

## 1. Identity & Session Management

Everything starts with a session. Opake supports multiple accounts and uses AT Protocol OAuth by default.

### Login

<CodeBlock language="sh">opake account login you.bsky.social</CodeBlock>

Override the PDS or fall back to legacy app-password auth:

<CodeBlock language="sh">opake account login you.bsky.social --pds https://pds.example.com</CodeBlock>

<CodeBlock language="sh">opake account login you.bsky.social --legacy</CodeBlock>

### Managing Accounts

<CodeBlock language="sh">opake account list</CodeBlock>

<CodeBlock language="sh">opake account set-default bob.other.com</CodeBlock>

Use a specific account for a single command with `--as`:

<CodeBlock language="sh">opake ls --as alice.example.com</CodeBlock>

---

## 2. The Social Filesystem

Managing your encrypted vault from the terminal.

### Upload & Download

<CodeBlock language="sh">opake upload photo.jpg --description "Beach vacation"</CodeBlock>

<CodeBlock language="sh">opake download photo.jpg -o ~/Downloads/copy.jpg</CodeBlock>

Decrypt and stream to stdout without saving locally:

<CodeBlock language="sh">opake cat notes.txt</CodeBlock>

### Organization

<CodeBlock language="sh">opake ls --long</CodeBlock>

<CodeBlock language="sh">opake mkdir Photos</CodeBlock>

<CodeBlock language="sh">opake tree</CodeBlock>

### Metadata

View or modify a document's metadata after upload:

<CodeBlock language="sh">opake metadata photo.jpg</CodeBlock>

<CodeBlock language="sh">opake metadata photo.jpg --rename "sunset.jpg"</CodeBlock>

<CodeBlock language="sh">opake metadata photo.jpg --add-tag vacation --add-tag beach</CodeBlock>

<CodeBlock language="sh">
  opake metadata photo.jpg --description "Golden hour at Scheveningen"
</CodeBlock>

---

## 3. Sharing & Collaboration

Cryptographic access control at your fingertips.

### Direct Sharing (Grants)

<CodeBlock language="sh">opake share new secret.pdf bob.bsky.social</CodeBlock>

<CodeBlock language="sh">opake share list</CodeBlock>

<CodeBlock language="sh">opake share inbox</CodeBlock>

<CodeBlock language="sh">opake share revoke at://did:plc:123/app.opake.grant/tid456</CodeBlock>

### Group Sharing (Workspaces)

<CodeBlock language="sh">opake workspace create "The Collective"</CodeBlock>

<CodeBlock language="sh">opake workspace add-member "The Collective" alice.bsky.social</CodeBlock>

<CodeBlock language="sh">opake upload internal-docs.zip --workspace "The Collective"</CodeBlock>

---

## 4. Maintenance & Security

### Device Pairing

<CodeBlock language="sh">opake pair request</CodeBlock>

Run the above on the **new** device, then approve on the **existing** device:

<CodeBlock language="sh">opake pair approve</CodeBlock>

### The Nuclear Option

<CodeBlock language="sh">opake account logout alice.bsky.social</CodeBlock>

<CodeBlock language="sh">opake rm -r /</CodeBlock>

<CodeBlock language="sh">opake purge --dry-run</CodeBlock>

<CodeBlock language="sh">opake purge --force</CodeBlock>

<Callout type="warning">
  **The Mini Nuke:** Running `opake rm -r /` clears your entire vault while keeping your
  cryptographic identity intact. Use it when you want a fresh start without re-pairing devices.
</Callout>

<Callout type="info">
  **Pro-Tip:** Every command supports `--help` for detailed usage and sub-command options.
</Callout>
